title: tool-handshake: resume streaming after function-call + weighted-stop/logprob fallback
author: Aisha Verma
release_notes: Improves /v1/chat.completions OpenAI compatibility: streaming resume after function/tool calls, better handling for stop arrays and weighted stop heuristics, safer logprob fallback when tokens are omitted. No customer-facing API change required; opt-in behind a compat flag for now.
description:
Context: customers reported unstable streams when a model emitted a tool/function call followed by immediate token streaming resume from a fallback model or when stop arrays and role aliases were present. This PR implements a more robust tool-handshake and stream-resume protocol that preserves OpenAI /v1/chat.completions semantics while enabling our internal optimizations.

What this changes: a) Introduces a handshake envelope for function/tool call boundaries so the stream can be cleanly suspended and resumed across model variants or retries; b) Adds a lightweight coordinator that computes weighted-stop heuristics and falls back to logprob-based termination when a stop sequence is partially emitted at stream boundaries; c) Normalizes role aliases (system/user/assistant) earlier in the pipeline to avoid duplicate role tokens in the prefill and while reconstructing deltas; d) Adds a compatibility gate (request header: X-OpenAI-Compat-V1) so customers can opt into v1-like behavior without changing their existing routing rules; e) Adds integration tests that simulate mid-stream fncall handoffs and partial stop sequences.

Implementation notes: the handshake is implemented as a framed JSON control message inserted between data CHUNKs. The coordinator maintains a small in-memory state machine per request (suspended, awaiting_ack, resumed) scoped to the connection ID. When a resume is requested and the target model cannot guarantee identical tokenization, we emit an idempotent resume envelope that instructs the client to rehydrate the last N tokens (configurable via compat param) or accept a logprob-fallback close. The weighted-stop heuristic computes candidate stop points across role boundaries and backfills stop-sentinels when the stream resumes to preserve deterministic termination behavior.

Backward compatibility: default behavior is unchanged. The new code path is behind the X-OpenAI-Compat-V1 header and a server-side feature flag. Migration plan includes a staged rollout, canary on 5% of production traffic, and a rollback knob.

Checklist:
- [x] Handshake envelope format and parsing implemented
- [x] Coordinator state machine with timeout and ack handling
- [x] Weighted-stop heuristic + logprob fallback path
- [x] Role alias normalization pass added to prefill
- [x] Integration + unit tests covering resume, partial stop, and fncall handoff
- [x] Documentation updated (compat guide + header semantics)

Related: Linear ENG-1984 tracks stream stability work. See SUP-8421 for customer incident that motivated this.

Summary of commits: single logical change implemented across runtime, api compatibility shim, and tests. Commits are squashed on merge.
commits: feat(streaming): add handshake envelope and resume flow
feat(api): compat header parsing and gate X-OpenAI-Compat-V1
fix(runtime): role alias normalizer to avoid duplicate prefill tokens
feat(coord): weighted-stop coordinator and logprob fallback
docs(compat): document handshake format and rollout notes

@@ go/runtime/streaming/handshake.go +12, -3
 func sendHandshake(conn *Conn, meta HandshakeMeta) error {
-    // previous naive resume
-    return conn.Write(controlResume(meta.TokenCursor))
+    env := Frame{Type: "control", Payload: meta} // new framed JSON envelope
+    return conn.Write(env.Encode())

review_comments: Jonah Kim: Left a couple of nit comments around timeouts and a question on whether the resume 'rehydrate N tokens' is safe across quantized kernels.
Aisha Verma (author): Answered - rehydrate N tokens is conservative (default 8) and is configurable per-route; added a test for cross-quantized-handoffs.
Lina Chen: Asked to add more logging fields (handoff_id, orig_model, target_model) to make postmortems easier. Requested a follow-up for perf impact analysis.
Mateo Ruiz: Approved after tests stabilized and CI flaked once but passed on rerun.
CI Bot: Integration tests passed (5/5), lint checks passed, flake detected in streaming integration on first run, reran and green.
discussion_summary: Main discussion centered on resume safety across tokenizer boundaries and how to surface the compat gate to customers.
Decided to keep default behavior unchanged and require explicit X-OpenAI-Compat-V1 header to opt in.
Follow-ups: add per-route perf telemetry (ENG-2003) and a backfill job to annotate historical logs with handshake events.
